title: Cap. XIV: Nullam extare in manuscriptis — printed rationes enough; MS survey opens
pass_a_gloss: CHAPTER XIV. That there exists in manuscript booklets no reason which can prove the immediate or antecedent imputation of Adam's sin. Concerning the arguments printed in type which it has fallen to me to read, it has been said, as I judge, enough. Of manuscripts I have seen many: but in which I have observed almost nothing that is not read in writings published by the work of printers; if you except that first one to which Placeus replied by that manuscript which D. Garissoles called the later one, and in refuting which he consumed a great part of his book.
pass_b_english: Chapter XIV. That no argument in the manuscript pamphlets can prove the immediate or antecedent imputation of Adam's sin. Of the printed arguments I have managed to read, enough has been said, I judge. I have seen many manuscripts, and in them I have noticed almost nothing that is not already in books issued by the printers—save that first piece to which Placeus answered in the manuscript Garissoles later called the later one, and on whose refutation Garissoles spent a great part of his book.
source_text: CAPUT XIV. Nullam extare in manuscriptis libellis rationem quae peccati Adamici imputationem immediatam seu antecedentem probare possit. De Argumentis typis excusis, quae mihi legere contigit, dictum est, ut ego arbitror, satis. Manuscriptorum vidi complura: Sed in quibus nihil fere animadverti, quod non legatur in scriptis Typographorum opera publicatis; si primum illud excipias, cui Placeus manuscripto illo respondit, quod D. Garissolius posterius appellavit, et in quo refellendo magnam partem libri sui consumpsit.
